source.title: Efficient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks

license.changes: Cropped from the original figure. Source colors and geometry are preserved.

teaching.spokenAnchor: In the StreamingLLM experiments, initial attention-sink tokens attracted attention even without useful semantic content. Keeping a few initial KV entries alongside recent tokens improved streaming stability for the evaluated models. The sink entries do not restore every evicted fact. Keep stability and distant-record retrieval as different tests.
teaching.moment: Show why retaining a few initial KV entries can stabilize a sliding cache without restoring evicted evidence.
teaching.scope: Keep the shown perplexities tied to the paper’s Llama-2-13B/PG19 experiment; sink stability is not fact retrieval.
teaching.caption: Source experiment: Llama-2-13B on PG19 (65K tokens). Sink stability does not restore evicted facts.
